findings.observation: The delivered How worker made one fffind call despite the explicit seven-tool-only assignment. The driver verified worker metadata and results without auditing worker-native calls.
findings.effect: The 146 passing machine checks do not establish a complete Perf workflow pass.
findings.observed_access: The FFF request selected the exact owned reader glob, an empty pattern and limit 100. The result contained ten owned relative filenames. No outside-repository source or network access was observed.
findings.repair_status: A future driver must bind live worker identities, audit all native attempts and explicitly declare accepted reader-tool paths and schemas. This audit does not retroactively authorize the call.

opening_a_pr.source: native Opening a PR stage in the unchanged machine receipt plus independent retained-artifact audit
observations: Owned stacked worktree starts at the exact open parent tip; one narrow conventional commit contains only reconcile.py and the portable PERFORMANCE.md.
Required original guidance and complete staged diff/stat review precede the commit; clean native statuses precede and follow the ready PR.
Origin absence is observed and gh fallback recorded before PR operations; one forge is used throughout.
One owned push and one ready child PR creation match independent exact head, base and body readback; the 27-line body reports measured results truthfully.
Remote head and PR inventories differ only by the owned branch and child PR; the parent and original local refs remain unchanged.
No merge, auto-merge, draft, babysit, hook/signature bypass or other forge mutation was observed.

limitations: The original machine PASS remains unchanged. Independent review rejects full Perf eligibility; this is not a fresh corrected-driver pass.
Standalone Opening a PR coverage does not make the earlier How protocol compliant and does not verify the remaining playbooks.
Worker identities were retrospectively matched within exact owned cwd sessions. No pre-dispatch reader-tree or live worker-actor UUID attestation was retained.
Observed owned-local search does not establish credential containment, pre-execution denial or absence of hidden application-level syscalls.
Measurements cover one deterministic workload on one host with process startup and warm filesystem effects; no general performance ceiling or production speedup is established.
Raw native sessions, configuration, private forge identities, binary profiles and worktrees stay private.
